question: Can a finite polynomial boundary record reconstruct every declared history, preserve all historical prefixes under extension, and correct a bounded symbol fault without confusing decoding with authenticity?
level: External finite arithmetic research; post-extension compatibility, not an endogenous breakthrough trial

scope.header: Trusted codec version, prime, history length and ordered sample locations
scope.fault_model: At most one substituted sample, OR at most two known erasures; header intact
scope.history_semantics: Ordered words over the declared alphabet only; no Rust SourceId, OccurrenceId, native History or certificate
scope.surface_geometry: Ordered sampling sites; no physical holographic duality, locality or continuous surface metric

imported_assumptions: Arithmetic is in the explicitly constructed prime field F_7.
A nonzero polynomial of degree below k has at most k-1 distinct roots.
All decoder guarantees are conditional on the trusted header and stated fault radius.
interface_justification: Original evaluation and interpolation code with an elementary root-count proof; equality of toy words does not allocate or identify Adva semantic objects.
protected_obligations: Retain chronological order, leading and trailing zero tokens and all old prefixes.
Keep boundary codewords separate from decoded words and partial observer projections.
No reduction modulo 7 of arbitrary external event identifiers.
No claimed authenticity from error correction alone.
No automatic field enlargement or fuel reset.

checker.single_faults: Clean word and every one-site nonzero additive fault at all five sites
checker.erasures: Every pair of missing sites for every length-three word
checker.extensions: Every length-three word and all seven appended symbols
checker.other_lengths: Every binary word of lengths zero through five
negative_controls: Two samples cannot distinguish a degree-two collision pair.
Per-domain projections can lose global order.
All-zero histories of different lengths require length metadata.
Repeated sample sites and out-of-alphabet symbols are rejected.
A sixth event is refused at the fixed one-error-correcting capacity.
Two substitutions can miscorrect to another valid history.
Two declared one-step continuation sets have different sizes but identical old-history readback.
checker.success: All declared checks and expected negative controls pass
checker.failure: Preserve last case, completed counts, digest and reason; no promotion of partial success

resources.enforcement: Fixed finite loops, explicit counters and per-decode fuel; a parent process applies timeout and POSIX CPU/address-space/file-size limits to the worker.
